ZB → CA / CH Supercell Viewer

The CuAu (CA) and chalcopyrite (CH) cells of CuInSe2 built from the zinc-blende ZnSe primitive cell, their Brillouin zones and k-paths, and the HSE06 phonon dispersions of CuInSe2, CuInS2 and their parents ZnSe and ZnS. Drag a crystal or a zone to rotate it; scroll or use ± to zoom.

Brillouin zones and standard k-paths

First Brillouin zones in the same cubic frame (k in units of 2π/a₀). The CA and CH zones sit inside the ZnSe zone (grey); their SeeK-path paths are labelled with the ZB point each one coincides with. Dashed arrows are the ordered-phase reciprocal-lattice vectors that fold ZB points onto Γ.

k-paths from SeeK-path (Hinuma et al., Comput. Mater. Sci. 128, 140 (2017)) using spglib (Togo et al., STAM Methods 4, 2384822 (2024)), for the ideal structures above. Folding to Γ: Xz = (0,0,1) in CA and CH; W = (0,1,½) and W′ = (1,0,½) in CH. Xx and Xy fold onto M in both phases.

Phonon dispersions (HSE06)

HSE06 force constants (FHI-aims + phonopy) interpolated with matdyn.x along the k-paths above. The LO–TO splitting uses the experimental ε∞ with the HSE06 Born charges. The parents ZnSe and ZnS were also computed in the CA and CH cells: their bands there are the zinc-blende bands folded into the smaller zone. Move the pointer over a plot to read off frequencies.

▶Animate any phonon mode: click any point of any dispersion below. The mode under the pointer then vibrates in the Mode animation panel at the end of this section, from where it can also be opened in the phonon website.

(a) ZB ZnSeprimitive cell · 2 atoms

(b) ZB ZnSprimitive cell · 2 atoms

Circles: the anion-only modes (only the anions move) at ○ Xz and ○ W. Folded onto Γ they become the totally symmetric A1 Raman modes of CA and CH, respectively. The Xz mode lies on the LA branch in ZnSe and on the LO branch in ZnS.

Supercell matrices. Rows give the ordered-phase vectors in the ZB basis a₁, a₂, a₃ (QE ibrav=2): MCA = [[−1,1,0],[0,0,1],[1,1,−1]], MCH = [[1,1,−2],[0,2,−1],[2,0,−1]]. |det M| counts the ZB primitive cells per ordered cell: 2 for CA (4 atoms), 4 for CH (8 atoms).

CA ordering. Alternating pure-Cu and pure-In (001) cation layers with period a₀. The cell is the square of side a₀/√2 inscribed in the cube base, rotated by 45°, with height a₀.

CH ordering. Each (001) cation layer is a Cu/In checkerboard, and Cu and In swap places from one layer to the next. The body-centred primitive cell spanned by c₁, c₂, c₃ is a sheared parallelepiped 3a₀ tall; the dashed box is the conventional a₀ × a₀ × 2a₀ cell (two primitive cells).
